mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 7.0% for three consecutive months, it signals persistent labor market weakness that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 7.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.01 over any 6-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate robust consumer demand and economic expansion, which together drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through improved corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their respective growth thresholds, or the interaction effect (measured by the product term) has a Rank IC below 0.02 over any 12-month window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of industrial production growth (INDPRO > 100), manufacturing activity expansion signals improving corporate capacity utilization and profit margins, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO exceeds 100, or the Rank IC for the INDPRO > 100 condition is below 0.02 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that boost household income and consumer spending, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS increases month-over-month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 6-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the core CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 233.0, it signals accelerating inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 233.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.01 over any 6-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 0.5%) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 233.0) indicate a monetary policy tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their thresholds, or the interaction term (FEDFUNDS * CPIAUCSL) has a Rank IC below 0.02 over any 12-month window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of slowing GDP growth (GDPC1 growth rate < 1.5% annualized), consumer and business confidence deteriorates, leading to reduced corporate investment and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where GDPC1 growth rate falls below 1.5% annualized, or the Rank IC for the slow growth condition is below 0.02 over any 12-month rolling window.
